consensus_summary: Primary settled meaning is Jesus Christ as the rejected stone who becomes the cornerstone/foundation of the church and a stumbling stone to unbelievers; common alternatives include believers as living stones, God as Rock/refuge, heart of stone, memorial stones, law tablets, and Daniel’s stone as Christ or kingdom.
book_summary: Stone means a person as a building member of a house or kingdom: Jesus the rejected living Stone made chief cornerstone, His people as living stones built under and aligned to Him, and the stone cut without hands as Christ the Head of the kingdom that grows into the mountain filling the earth.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ as rejected cornerstone/foundation (and relatedly stumbling stone)
book_core_identification: A person as building member of house/kingdom (Christ the cornerstone plus His people as living stones; Daniel stone = Christ as kingdom Head)
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates believers-as-living-stones and the Daniel kingdom-stone into the same primary building-member identification with Christ, while de-emphasizing or omitting consensus alternatives (stumbling-stone emphasis as distinct, God-as-Rock, heart of stone, memorials, law tablets, Matt 16:18 Peter).
rationale: Consensus primary (Christ cornerstone from Ps 118/Isa 28/NT applications) and its most common alternative (living stones) are preserved and united under the book’s single category ‘person as building member,’ with Daniel’s stone read as Christ/Head of the growing kingdom—readings already present in the consensus. This keeps the same central referents but broadens and re-scopes the core from ‘Christ primarily’ to a unified Christ-and-people building/kingdom frame, changing extension and precision without replacing the referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus treats Christ-as-cornerstone as the distinct primary and living stones/Daniel kingdom as secondary; folding them into one generic ‘person as building member’ core could be seen as over-broadening or re-ranking rather than equivalent.
